title: Inventory Ledger Integrity for Logistics
business: A global logistics provider managing high-velocity warehouse inventory.
problem: Direct modification of raw inventory counts by disparate microservices leads to race conditions and inconsistent stock levels, causing shipping delays and manual reconciliation overhead.
solution: Encapsulation hides the mutable inventory state behind a controlled public boundary, ensuring that all stock adjustments pass through a validated business logic layer that enforces atomic updates.
steps: Define a private state object to hold raw inventory quantities.
Expose only a public interface for incrementing or decrementing stock.
Implement internal validation logic within the public methods to reject invalid states.
Restrict direct access to the raw state using language-level access modifiers.
Expose a read-only snapshot of the current state for reporting purposes.
outcome: Improved system reliability through predictable state transitions and a centralized audit trail for all inventory modifications.
limitation: The primary tradeoff is increased boilerplate code and potential latency due to the mandatory validation layer; check for this by monitoring the execution time of interface methods against raw state access patterns.

To remove the need for an audit log in the warehouse system.
questions.explanation: The problem states that direct modification leads to inconsistencies, which encapsulation solves by forcing all changes through a controlled boundary.
